 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. MIAMI – Walter Clayton Jr. signed a two-way contract with the Dallas Mavericks last Wednesday and was active for the team's season opener in Houston within hours.
 It didn't take long for an opportunity to arise for the former No. 18 overall pick of the 2025 NBA draft .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Clayton's debut at American Airlines Center provided a glimpse of why the Mavericks coveted his services once he was waived by the Memphis Grizzlies. He scored three points, grabbed three rebounds, dished out five assists and came away with a steal in 15 minutes of action in Saturday's loss to San Antonio.
 "It's been a seamless transition," Clayton said after Monday's shootaround in Miami. "It ain't been too hard. It's actually been pretty smooth."
 The Mavericks entered the season with a need for guard depth, to supplement the production offered by Kyrie Irving , Sergio De Larrea and Marcus Sasser . On nights when Irving rests, as he did on Saturday, there will be chances for Dallas' young guards to showcase their abilities.
 With a lack of first-round draft assets, the Mavericks front office duo of Masai Ujiri and Mike Schmitz are taking fliers on former first-round picks. They traded for former 2024 No. 1 pick Zaccharie Risacher and Sasser, the 25th pick in the 2023 draft. They also signed former lottery pick Jett Howard to a two-way contract before the start of training camp.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Clayton is the latest example of their creative strategy, with the hopes of uncovering the untapped potential in young prospects who could thrive in a new environment. With Clayton on a two-way deal, he'll spend time with both the Mavericks and Texas Legends. He is only allotted 50 games of eligibility on the active list for the Mavericks, who will need to be strategic about his usage.
 What are the Mavericks asking from him?
 "Just be a good lead guard, make sure the team is organized whenever I'm on the floor, hit shots," Clayton said. "I think that's it. Make sure everybody's involved."
 Clayton played 24 games for the Grizzlies after he was dealt by the Utah Jazz as part of the blockbuster trade for Jaren Jackson Jr. He averaged 9.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 5.7 assists while shooting 36.6% from 3-point range in that span.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I think last year was an up-and-down year," Clayton said. "I only take it as a learning year. I think we go through everything for a reason. I'm thankful for last year and I'm glad to be here in Dallas."
